evidence.reason: At current line 148, `pythonNumberText` uses `String(value)`, so an integral float such as `1` becomes `"1"` rather than the documented Python `repr(float)` text `"1.0"` (and JS exponent spelling also differs from Python). Feeding that raw text back through `parseJsonValue` therefore loses float-vs-int semantics. The function comment explicitly says it returns the Python `repr(float)` text used by `JsonNumber.float`, so this is an implementation defect in intended behavior, not a new requirement.
